question: partner-distribution
summary: For a one-person AI agent builder, the three voice-platform partner programs (Retell, Vapi, Telnyx) publish no application fee and no commission rate: they offer directory listings, lead routing, co-marketing and tiered benefits, so the revenue has to come from buying usage at published pay-as-you-go rates and reselling it at a markup (inference from the published price lists). The vertical software channels are scale-gated instead — Clio requires 100 active customer accounts for its Silver tier, Intuit charges $300-$4,500/month by tier and requires 500 active connections for Gold — and Vantaca's partner page is written for companies that integrate into its platform and 'co-build the integration', so it is not an obvious entry channel for a services-only firm with no clients. The realistic near-term distribution is referral: recruit local referrers who already sell to the same small businesses (legal IT consultants and bookkeepers, insurance-agency IT support firms, phone/telecom installers, web agencies) and pay them roughly 10-20% of first-year collected revenue, which brackets the 20% median across the 147 referral programs in a 556-program benchmark that publish a rate. Evidence also warns against over-weighting badges: a 97-agency study found 17 agencies displaying vendor partner badges with no publicly documented client from those partnerships, while 58% of 173 Clutch reviews of AI agencies named a referral or personal network as the project origin.

findings.finding: Retell's Solution Partner Program is a directory/lead-routing program, not a published revenue-share program; membership requirements and tier thresholds are not public.
findings.evidence: The Retell partner docs page lists benefits as 'Access to Qualified Leads' (Retell refers potential customers to certified partners), website 'Find a Partner' visibility, co-marketing for higher-tier partners, and early access to features/betas. The partner portal adds profile management, auto-sync with the directory, agent templates, lead management and client reviews, and says partners can 'track leads and see your tier standing' — no commission, minimum client count or fee is stated anywhere on the public pages.

findings.finding: Retell's separate affiliate program pays 15% of a referral's revenue for 12 months, with a 90-day cookie and monthly payouts, and referral sign-ups do not count toward Solution Partner tiers.
findings.evidence: The affiliate page states: 'earn 15% of every referral's revenue for 12 months', '90-day cookie window', 'Monthly payouts ... no thresholds'. Its FAQ answers 'Do referral signups count toward Solution Partner tiers?' with 'No — only accounts you actively build and manage count toward Solution Partner tiers. If you start managing a referred account, you can convert it.' No joining fee is stated on the page.

findings.finding: Retell's published cost stack leaves room for resale margin: $0.07-$0.31 per minute on pay-as-you-go, plus small per-number and concurrency charges, while BAA/SSO/custom MSA are enterprise-only; Retell's own partner guidance says to price services separately from usage and treat commission and minimum deal sizes as vendor questions.
findings.evidence: Pricing page lists 'Voice AI: $0.07-$0.31/minute' pay-as-you-go (custom pricing for Enterprise), 20 concurrent calls included then $8.00/concurrency/month, Retell phone numbers $2.00/month, verified numbers $10.00/month, telephony $0.015/min, and HIPAA/BAA, SSO, custom MSA/DPA/BAA shown only in the Enterprise column. Retell's partner scoping post (separate URL, https://www.retellai.com/blog/voice-ai-partner-deal-scoping) says services should be 'priced separately from usage' and that 'Commission, minimum deal sizes and vendor services pricing are questions to agree with the vendor, not assumptions to build into a quote.'

findings.finding: Vapi's Solutions Partner Program offers enablement and co-selling but publishes no commission, reseller discount or white-label terms.
findings.evidence: The partnerships page describes Solution Partners as 'specialized consultancies, global systems integrators, and agencies' who design flows and integrate Vapi, with benefits of a dedicated partner manager and Slack channel, solution design reviews, templates/playbooks/demo environments, co-selling 'on qualified deals', roadmap previews and early access. No percentage, fee or minimum is stated; the page ends with an application form.

findings.finding: Vapi's cost floor is $0.05/minute hosting plus model pass-through, but production and compliance tiers add fixed monthly costs that matter for a solo firm ($29 Core, $999/month Pro minimum, $2,000/month HIPAA).
findings.evidence: Pricing page: no-package usage at '$0.05/min Vapi hosting. Models pass-through at cost'; Core $29/month; Pro '10% of Vapi hosting fee, $999/mo minimum'; HIPAA compliance add-on '$2,000/month'; additional concurrency $10/line/month; additional organizations $20/month. Its worked example for 1,000 minutes/month totals $82-$129/month.

findings.finding: Vapi's 15% referral program is aimed at content creators, not agencies, and bundles free minutes and beta access rather than a reseller margin.
findings.evidence: The Creators page lists perks by tier: 'Up to 5K+ Vapi minutes', '15% referral revenue', 'Beta feature access and priority Slack support', and 'Vapi users via newsletter, socials etc.'; the how-it-works steps are apply, create content, grow.

findings.finding: Telnyx runs one partner program with channel/referral, agency and distributor tracks, promising 'competitive commissions' and volume-based rewards, but publishes no rate, tier threshold or minimum.
findings.evidence: The partner page describes 'Channel and referral' ('resell Telnyx services, refer qualified leads, or act as a strategic advisor ... competitive commissions'), 'Agencies' (white-label capabilities, co-marketing) and 'Distributors', plus 'Earn competitive commissions and unlock volume-based rewards'; its closing section names 'the Telnyx Amplify Partner Program'. No percentage, tier threshold or minimum appears. The launch release that gives the date and tier language is a separate page (https://rss.globenewswire.com/news-release/2025/06/10/3096944/0/en/Telnyx-Launches-Partner-Program-to-Accelerate-Growth-in-Real-Time-Voice-AI-and-Connectivity-Solutions.html, 10 June 2025): it says 'Tiered offerings match varying levels of engagement and capability' and that 'The Telnyx Partner Program is now open to select partners', calls it 'a new Partner Program', and states no rate.

findings.finding: Clio's app program is gated by installed base: Silver requires at least 100 active Clio customer accounts and Gold is invite-only, so a no-client firm cannot enter it as a partner.
findings.evidence: Clio's developer docs list Silver requirements including 'Have at least 100 active Clio customer accounts', 99.5% uptime on a 30-day rolling basis, one-business-day support turnaround, Google Lighthouse score of at least 50, security assessment, and a demo with Clio's App Ecosystem team; Gold requires an invitation and all Silver requirements. Benefits include Clio sales/support teams recommending the app and inclusion in an internal partner database used by Clio Sales (Silver+).

findings.finding: Getting listed in Clio's App Directory itself is a review process (security questionnaire + recorded demo + listing form), with no listing fee stated — but it is for software integrations, not service providers.
findings.evidence: Clio's launch guide describes: Step 1 complete Clio's security and compliance questionnaire (request via api.partnerships@clio.com for Clio Manage), Step 2 email a pre-recorded demo to the API Partnerships team, Step 3 the team provides an App Directory listing form and drafts the listing, Step 4 launch. No fee or revenue share is mentioned on the page.

findings.finding: MyCase recruits legal accounting, bookkeeping, business and IT consultants to refer small law firms, paying 10% of ACV at entry and promoting them to a directory listing at 3 and 20 subscriptions.
findings.evidence: The Consultant Program page addresses 'legal accounting, bookkeeping, business, and IT professionals'. Referral Partner: 'Earn 10% of ACV with annual contract', 'Earn 5% of ACV with monthly sign up', 'One time commission when you submit firm as a lead', 'No training or minimum requirements'. Certified Consultant is 'Earned after 3 new account subscriptions and basic training completed' with 'Listing in our certified consultant directory' and 'Earn a higher rate of commission'; Gold Certified is 'Earned after 20 new user subscriptions and advanced training completed' with 'the highest commission available'. The specific higher percentages and any fee are not printed on the page.

findings.finding: Vantaca's partner program is written for technology providers that integrate into its community-association platform, offering integration support and co-marketing rather than a referral fee; it publishes no fee, revenue share or application steps.
findings.evidence: The become-a-partner page frames the offer as 'the platform behind 50,000+ associations' and lists 50K+ associations managed, 6.5M+ homeowners and 16K+ CAM professionals. Integration surfaces named are HOAi Fleet ('An agentic AI workforce that handles AP, AR, financial production, board packets, and association onboarding autonomously'), Vantaca Home and Vantaca Vendor. Promised support is 'a dedicated point of contact, technical integration support, and a structured onboarding process', with co-marketing and 'direct access to the management companies making buying decisions'. No application steps, NDA, contract terms, fees or commission rates appear on the page. Inference (not stated on the page): because it describes partners who 'co-build the integration, co-launch it, and stay involved after go-live', a services-only firm may be gated.

findings.finding: Vantaca promotes a half-day partner certification session with a badge and co-marketing priority, and publishes no price or eligibility rule for it.
findings.evidence: The certification page advertises 'In a half day at Vantaca HQ' with a Vantaca Certified Partner credential and digital badge, priority co-marketing access, and a session at the Hyatt Regency New Orleans (601 Loyola Ave), November 2, 2026, 8:00 a.m. - 11:00 a.m., 'only 20 seats per session'. It also promises early access to roadmap updates and 'a direct line into the Vantaca team'. No fee, prerequisite (such as an existing integration) or eligibility rule is printed on the page.

findings.finding: Applied Systems opened a formal Vendor Certification Program in August 2026 for integrations into Applied Epic, and separately lists 'Preferred Consultants' that include IT support and security providers serving agencies.
findings.evidence: The August 12, 2026 release announces the Vendor Certification Program as 'a clear, single path to certification', with certified integrations 'faster than a standard integration build' and requiring 'no additional purchase from Applied'; vendors apply via vendor-requests@appliedsystems.com, and the release names the first certified companies (Ascend, Adapt, Coverflow, Fulcrum and others). The integrations-partners directory has a separate 'Preferred consultants for Applied Epic' section: 'Preferred consultants work with your agency on Applied Epic workflows, accounting and bookkeeping, IT, security and staffing', each with 'direct access to Applied Epic and other Applied products'; listed firms include Archway Computer ('a premier IT support provider ... tailored for independent insurance agencies') and Advantage Microsystems.

findings.finding: The QuickBooks/Intuit marketplace is a paid, scale-gated channel: Builder is free but capped, Silver is $300/month, Gold $1,700/month with 500+ active connections, Platinum $4,500/month with 3,000+.
findings.evidence: Intuit's App Partner Program Guide (v1.2_03.2026) sets Program Fees of 'Builder: No charge', 'Silver US$300', 'Gold US$1,700', 'Platinum US$4,500' per month, with Builder capped at 500,000 CorePlus API credits and above-cap calls blocked, variable CorePlus API fees beyond credits ($3.50/1K at Silver up to 10M calls), Gold requiring 'a minimum of 500 Minimum Active Connections' and Platinum 'a minimum of 3000'. Marketplace listing only appears from the Silver tier up.

findings.finding: Most partner programs do not publish a rate; among those that do, the median referral commission is 20% and the middle half falls between 17.5% and 30%.
findings.evidence: Promethean Research's dataset of 556 verified programs across 33 vendor categories (verified July 2026) reports: 37% (203) publish a commission, discount or margin as a percentage; referral is the lead model for 268 programs, of which 147 publish a percentage, with a median of 20% and a middle half between 17.5% and 30%; only 19% (106) state that payments recur; 63% (353) publish no comparable percentage. It also notes a 10% commission paid for three years produces 50% more revenue than a 20% one-time commission on the same annual spend.

findings.finding: Referral is the most commonly documented client source for AI agencies, while vendor partner badges show no documented clients in a 97-agency study.
findings.evidence: Redictos' AI Agency Market Study 2026 (97 agencies: 38 US/UK, 49 DACH, 10 Spain; 173 Clutch reviews across 20 agencies, collected 5-6 October 2026) reports 58% of reviews (100 of 173) name a referral or personal network as the project origin versus 27% online search (47) and 5% directories/freelance platforms (9); '17 agencies display partner badges from vendors such as OpenAI, HubSpot, Make or Zapier. None has a documented client from that partnership.' It also reports US/UK medians of about EUR 2,000 for an entry offer (n=16), EUR 4,300 for a build (n=11), and EUR 2,900/month for a managed agent/retainer (n=11), with maintenance-only under EUR 500/month (n=5).

findings.finding: Phone/telecom resellers are an established referral channel with published residual norms of roughly 8-25% depending on model, which sets the range to beat when recruiting phone-system installers.
findings.evidence: VoIP International's 2026 guide states rates of 8-15% of what the master agent receives for sub-agents, 10-20% for carrier direct agents, and 15-25% for direct referral partners, and argues 'rate x duration x reliability is the real formula' because 12-36-month commission sunsets are common; its own program pays 100% of the first month then 20% for the life of the account, paid by the 15th.

findings.finding: Restaurant POS integration partnership is a multi-month engineering path (security/legal approval, partner agreement, certification call, alpha with one restaurant, beta with 3-5 locations) — not a quick channel for food businesses.
findings.evidence: Toast's developer guide on the integration partnership process requires approval from Toast's compliance, privacy, security and legal teams, a signed partner agreement, an assigned Toast integration team representative, sandbox development, a one-hour certification review, then an alpha and 'a beta with roughly three to five locations' before general availability; it notes Toast 'receives a high volume of applications ... and is not able to integrate with all interested integration partners'.

resources.name: Retell AI Solution Partner Program (application + partner portal)
resources.what_it_offers: Application to be listed in Retell's 'Find a Partner' directory with profile management, agent templates, lead management, client reviews, tier standing, and (at higher tiers) co-marketing.
resources.how_to_use_it: Apply once you have one live agent and a client reference or demo; keep the listing aimed at your verticals and log every lead the portal routes so you can judge whether directory leads are real for you.

resources.name: Retell Affiliate Program
resources.what_it_offers: 15% of a referred customer's revenue for 12 months, 90-day cookie, monthly payouts, no thresholds.
resources.how_to_use_it: Register before your first client conversation so any client who wants to own their own Retell account still pays you a year of commission; do not rely on it for accounts you manage (those belong to the partner tiers instead).

resources.name: Vapi Solutions Partner Program
resources.what_it_offers: Dedicated partner manager and Slack channel, solution design reviews, templates/playbooks/demo environments, co-selling on qualified deals, roadmap previews.
resources.how_to_use_it: Apply after picking one vertical use case, so the application can describe a repeatable offering rather than a generic agency pitch; ask in writing for commission, deal registration and minimums, which are not on the page.

resources.name: Telnyx Amplify Partner Program
resources.what_it_offers: Channel/referral, agency and distributor tracks; 'competitive commissions' with volume-based rewards, technical enablement, co-marketing and sales/training resources.
resources.how_to_use_it: Use it as the telephony/SIP layer option and price check against Retell's built-in telephony ($0.015/min); request the rate card and reseller discount schedule during the partner conversation, since neither page publishes one.

resources.name: Clio API Partnerships / Certified App Program
resources.what_it_offers: App Directory listing (security review + recorded demo), then Silver tier with sales-team enablement, an assigned App Partnerships Manager and marketing eligibility once at 100+ active Clio accounts.
resources.how_to_use_it: Treat as a year-2 goal. For now, use Clio's directory to study which intake/document tools law firms already install, and build your agent to write into those rather than chasing a listing.

resources.name: MyCase Consultant Program (via PartnerStack)
resources.what_it_offers: Referral Partner: 10% of ACV on annual contracts, 5% on monthly sign-ups, no training or minimums; Certified Consultant after 3 subscriptions plus basic training (directory listing, badge, higher unpublished rate); Gold after 20 subscriptions plus advanced training.
resources.how_to_use_it: Sign up as a Referral Partner as a cash side-channel and a legitimate reason to be in conversation with small law firms; the same relationships are your pilot pipeline for intake agents.

resources.name: Vantaca Partner Program and Partner Certification
resources.what_it_offers: Integration partner track for the CAM platform (50K+ associations, 16K+ CAM professionals) with dedicated contact, technical integration support, structured onboarding and co-marketing; certification is a half-day session with a digital badge and priority co-marketing.
resources.how_to_use_it: Certification session: November 2, 2026, 8:00-11:00 a.m., Hyatt Regency New Orleans, 20 seats per session. Before spending on travel, ask in writing whether a services-only partner (no software integration) is accepted — the pages do not say.

resources.name: Applied Systems Vendor Certification Program
resources.what_it_offers: Single path to certify an integration with Applied Epic; certified vendors get current Epic releases and agencies can activate without an extra Applied purchase; vendors also appear in the partners directory alongside 'Preferred Consultants'.
resources.how_to_use_it: Email vendor-requests@appliedsystems.com early to ask what certification involves for a small vendor — and separately scan the Preferred Consultants list for insurance-focused IT providers to approach as referrers.

resources.name: Intuit App Partner Program
resources.what_it_offers: QuickBooks Online API access with four tiers; Builder is free with no monetary commitment and 500,000 CorePlus API credits/month; Silver adds marketplace listing, demand generation, referral management and uncapped API calls with fees above credits.
resources.cost: Builder no charge; Silver US$300/month; Gold US$1,700/month; Platinum US$4,500/month (Program Fees, per the Program Guide)
resources.how_to_use_it: Stay on Builder while prototyping a bookkeeping/document agent; do not subscribe to Silver until you have paying users, since marketplace listing is the only thing the fee buys that you need later.

resources.name: Toast Integration Partner application
resources.what_it_offers: Formal path to a certified restaurant POS integration: application vetting, compliance/privacy/security/legal approval, partner agreement, sandbox, certification call, alpha and beta.
resources.how_to_use_it: For food businesses in year one, partner with local POS resellers/installers instead; revisit Toast only if a restaurant client demands a native integration.

resources.name: Free referral partner agreement template (partner.io)
resources.what_it_offers: 11-section US referral agreement template with a Schedule A fee table: referral acceptance and first-come rule, 90-day default protection period, fee on net collected revenue, clawbacks for refunds, W-9 before payment, and post-termination payment for pre-existing referrals.
resources.cost: Free, no sign-up (Word .docx download); updated October 7, 2026
resources.how_to_use_it: Use it as the base for your first two or three referrer agreements (fill in your state as governing law and a 10-20% fee); it is written for B2B software subscriptions, so adapt the product language to a services pilot, and have a lawyer review it before scaling beyond a handful of partners.

resources.name: Promethean Research agency partner program rate data
resources.what_it_offers: Published analysis of 556 verified partner programs across 33 categories: which publish rates, median referral rate (20%), recurrence rates, and a worksheet of fields to compare offers (model, rate, earning period, attribution, work required).
resources.cost: Article free; full 556-program directory pricing not public
resources.how_to_use_it: Use the free analysis to sanity-check any rate a vertical vendor offers you, and copy its comparison fields into a one-page spreadsheet for each program you evaluate.

recommendations_for_us: Inference: treat platform partner programs as credibility and lead-flow, not as revenue. Retell, Vapi and Telnyx publish benefits but no commission rate, and the 97-agency study found 17 agencies with vendor badges and no publicly documented client from them — so budget zero revenue from directory leads and judge each program after 90 days on actual inquiries.

Inference: earn margin on usage, not commission. Retell pay-as-you-go is $0.07-$0.31/minute and Vapi is $0.05/minute hosting plus model pass-through, so quote clients a per-minute or per-outcome price that covers usage plus your care fee; this is the only reliably published economics in the voice stack.

Inference: avoid compliance-heavy clients in year one. A BAA is Enterprise-only at Retell and a $2,000/month add-on at Vapi, which would swamp a small pilot — favor law-firm intake, contractor dispatch and property-management calls over anything touching patient data.

Inference: build the referral bench before the product is finished. Target 3-5 referrers who already sell to our exact buyers and do not build agents: legal IT consultants and bookkeepers (MyCase pays referral partners 10% of ACV at entry and certified consultants a higher, unpublished rate), insurance-agency IT support firms listed as Applied 'Preferred Consultants', telecom/phone installers (whose own residual norms run 8-25%), and small web agencies. Offer 10-20% of first-year collected revenue, which brackets the 20% median and sits below the telecom direct-referral range of 15-25%.

Inference: pay on collected revenue, cap the term, and use a 90-day protection window. The published template's structure (net collected revenue, clawbacks, W-9, post-termination tail) protects a one-person firm from paying on churned pilots; partner.io's own framing is that most referral disputes are about who sent the referral rather than the terms, and Promethean lists attribution as one of four checks to run before referring a real opportunity (window, deal registration, existing-account exclusions, duplicate claims, dispute process).

Inference: use MyCase's consultant program as a low-cost warm-up in legal. No fee or minimum is published for the entry tier, it gives a legitimate reason to meet small firms, and it converts the same relationships into intake-agent pilots later — but do not build an app for Clio's directory yet, since Silver requires 100 active Clio accounts.

Inference: for property management, do not lead with a back-office agent. Vantaca already ships 'HOAi Fleet' for AP/AR and board packets, and its partner page is written for companies that integrate into its platform and 'co-build the integration' — so a services-only firm may be gated there. Target management companies on other stacks, or sell the phone/intake layer that feeds whatever system they already run.

Inference: skip Intuit's paid tiers and Toast's engineering track for now. Intuit Silver is $300/month and Gold $1,700/month with 500+ connections; Toast requires legal review, certification and an alpha/beta. Use bookkeepers as referrers and POS installers as referrers rather than becoming a marketplace developer in year one.

Inference: instrument attribution from the first conversation. The agency study found only 4 of 24 agencies ask prospects how they found them; a single 'how did you hear about us' field plus a shared referral form is the minimum needed to know whether the referrer bench or the directory is actually working.

pitfalls.pitfall: Assuming a partner program pays a commission: 63% of 556 verified programs publish no comparable percentage, and Retell, Vapi and Telnyx all describe benefits without rates.
Confusing a reseller discount with a referral commission or white-label margin — a 20% referral fee and a 20% discount apply to different revenue and require very different work.
Chasing marketplace certification before having customers: Clio Silver needs 100 active Clio accounts and Intuit Gold needs 500 active connections.
Underestimating fixed platform costs: Intuit Silver is $300/month and Gold $1,700/month before any customer pays you.
Taking on health-adjacent work without pricing compliance: a BAA is Enterprise-only at Retell, and Vapi's HIPAA add-on is $2,000/month.
Treating a partner badge as distribution — 17 AI agencies displayed vendor badges with no documented client from the partnership.

Paying referral fees on invoiced rather than collected revenue, which leaves you paying on pilots that churn; the published template ties fees to net revenue actually collected and adds clawbacks for a reason.

Assuming a vertical incumbent has left you space: Vantaca's own platform ships an 'agentic AI workforce' for AP, AR, board packets and onboarding, the same back-office work we would sell to property managers.

caveats: All program terms were read on 12 November 2026; partner programs change terms and tiers without notice (Clio and Intuit both reserve the right to change requirements and fees).

Several programs deliberately keep commercial terms off the public web (Retell partner tiers, Vapi commissions, Telnyx rates, Vantaca and Applied fees), so 'not public' here means not published, not zero; the same applies to joining fees — no page read states an application fee of $0.

The Telnyx partner page reflects the program as of 2026; its launch date, the 'select partners' wording and the tier language come from Telnyx's 10 June 2025 GlobeNewswire release, and the release does not use the name 'Amplify' (the current partner page does).

The Redictos study is an observational analysis of public sources (Clutch reviews, agency websites, ads libraries) over 97 agencies, mostly small AI agencies; 'no documented client' means not publicly provable, not proof the channel fails.
Promethean Research is a research firm that sells a 556-program directory; its benchmark is descriptive of programs that publish rates, not a random sample of all vendors.
The telecom commission figures come from a vendor's own explainer (VoIP International), which has an interest in framing typical rates; treat them as directional.

Marketplace requirements quoted here are those of the software vendors, and none of these pages say whether a services-only firm (implementation/consulting without a software product) can join the app or certification tracks.
data_gaps: Retell Solution Partner tier thresholds and any commission or discount are not published; the partner portal requires sign-in, so requirements could not be verified.

Telnyx's partner application form asks for business details, partnership type, budget, geographies, sales-rep and sales-engineer counts and pipeline, but sits behind a login page (partners.telnyx.com) that could not be read.
MyCase's Certified Consultant and Gold commission percentages are described only as 'higher'/'highest'; the numbers are not printed on the public page.
Vantaca publishes no application steps, NDA or contract terms, fees or revenue share; whether a services-only firm can join, and whether certification costs anything, is unverified.
Applied Systems' certification cost, timeline and eligibility for non-software consultants are not published; there is no public 'preferred consultant' application page.
Clio does not state whether any listing or certification fee exists, and whether a services-only partner can be listed in the App Directory.
Toast's main partner page (pos.toasttab.com/partners) returned HTTP 403; only the developer-process documentation was readable, and no referral/channel-partner commission terms were found.
Two r/msp threads on partnering with an AI consultant and on approaching MSPs for referral agreements could not be retrieved (JavaScript/blocked), so no first-hand MSP account is included.
The eForms consultant referral agreement template returned HTTP 403; only the partner.io template could be verified.
No NJ-specific data was found on local referral-partner norms, Middlesex County MSP counts, or local chamber/broker referral practices.
No evidence was found on how often small firms (5-200 staff) actually buy AI agents through a platform partner directory; the only channel data found is agency-level and public-source based.
